title: Extremely good 2d models with Gemini 3.8 flash extended
author: Accomplished-Fan9568
selftext: **How to make sweet 2d models with gemini 3.8 flash extended** So other than the prompt, you want to specify what model u want also, and provide a reference image, for my game i use top down images, heres my USS Fletcher it turned out great imo. I've successfully made several models now actually. In fact I was hoping we could make a community project if anyone is interested, WW2 Naval / Battlefield style in 2d. You can write me a private message if it sounds like a cool idea, if not I will continue making it myself but more slowly. Anyway enjoy! Prompt: (you must add a subject and a reference image to gemini) I have attached a reference image of a [insert subject, e.g., spaceship, car, guitar]. Write a single-file HTML/JS document using the HTML5 Canvas 2D API to render a highly accurate, procedural 2D model of this subject. Technical and Rendering Requirements: Zero Assets: Do not use tags, external assets, or SVG files. The entire model must be drawn programmatically using Canvas API paths, shapes, and curves. Responsive Canvas: Create a full-screen layout with a neutral studio background. The canvas must handle high-DPI displays cleanly and automatically scale the model to fit 85% of the screen, keeping it perfectly centered on window resize. Class Structure: Encapsulate the drawing logic inside a JavaScript class (e.g., ProceduralModel). Normalized Coordinate System: Do not hardcode absolute pixel positions. Use a normalized coordinate system (from 0.0 to 1.0) for the length and width of the subject. Plot all components, curves, and details as percentages of the total length/width so the model maintains exact proportions at any scale. Layering and Depth: Break the drawing sequence into logical layers (e.g., lower appendages, main body, upper details). Lighting and Texture: Sample the colors from the attached reference image. Use multi-stop linear and radial CanvasGradient objects to simulate 3D volume, metallic/matte textures, and ambient occlusion.

Let me know what you think and see if it works for you; you can check the files by clicking "Edit."

replies.author: Accomplished-Fan9568
replies.body: Neat but what is it for?

replies.author: ChocolateTemporary48
replies.body:
When I created it, the goal was to prepare designs for the game \*Naval Art\*.



I also wanted to try making my own version of another game called \*Rule the Waves\*.



I wanted to share it with you in case it could serve as inspiration—perhaps for creating a similar system that allows for custom ship designs.
